chunks: My father (RA) narrated to us, he said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu 'Abdillah (AS)
He said: "He who claims that Allah, the Mighty and High, is in a thing or from a thing or on a thing, has told a lie."

The Compiler of this book (RA) said: The proof that Allah, the Mighty and High, is not in a place is that all places are created (hadith). The proof has been established that Allah, the Mighty and High, is Eternal (Qadim), preceding places. It is not permissible that the Self-Sufficient Eternal One needs what He was Self-Sufficient from, nor that He changes from what He has always been upon. Thus, it is correct today that He is not in a place, just as He has always been so. The confirmation of this is:
ai.seo_question: What is the proof that Allah is not in a specific place according to al-Tawhid?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) declares that attributing spatial location to Allah is falsehood, a doctrine central to Shia theological debates against the Mu'tazila and Ash'aris regarding divine attributes. Shaykh al-Saduq elucidates this by arguing that since space (al-makan) is a created entity, the Eternal God cannot be confined within it or require it, thereby affirming His transcendence beyond physical dimensions. This reasoning underscores the principle that God's essence is independent of the created order, rejecting any form of corporealism or spatial containment.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 10. My father (RA) said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Mahbub, on the authority of Hammad ibn `Amr, that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:
“Verily, whoever claims that Allah, the Mighty and High, is in a thing or from a thing or on a thing ahs uttered a lied.”

The Compiler (RA) of this book says: The proof that Allah, the Mighty and High, is not in space is that space is caused. The proof has already been established that Allah, that the Mighty and High, is without beginning, and existed prior to the existence of space. It is not permissible to say that the Self-Sufficient [Ghani] without Beginning [Qadim] may be in need of anything, nor that He may change from what He has always been.
